programs.name: subraid
programs.purpose: Merge ordered traces from multiple files into one ordered stream.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: SUBRAID - Braid traces from files together and output.

params.name: in0 through in99
params.description: Input SU filenames; at least two distinct inMM parameters are required.

params.name: key
params.description: Ordered header keys; prefix a key with - for descending order or + for ascending order.

params.name: trac
params.description: Set to 1 to renumber tracl and tracr, or 0 to retain them.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Header values are converted to double and multiplied by the ordering direction before comparison. NaN header values do not compare in the usual total order. On failure to read a file's first trace, idf[nfiles] is used before initialization.
programs.difficulty_reason: It performs a multiway ordered merge with one buffered trace per input and checks ordering as it writes.

test_cases.description: Merge two files by trace number and retain their original trace counters.
test_cases.command: suplane nt=64 ntr=4 > in1.su && suplane nt=64 ntr=3 > in2.su && subraid in1=in1.su in2=in2.su key=tracl trac=0 > out.su

test_cases.description: Merge three files using two ascending keys and renumber output traces.
test_cases.command: suplane nt=64 ntr=4 > in1.su && suplane nt=64 ntr=4 > in2.su && suplane nt=64 ntr=2 > in3.su && subraid in0=in1.su in4=in2.su in9=in3.su key=tracl,cdp trac=1 > out.su

programs.name: sucleave
programs.purpose: Split an input trace stream into files according to ranges of a header value.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: SUCLEAVE - Cleave traces from 1 input into multiple output files.

params.name: key
params.description: Header key used to assign traces to output ranges.

params.name: abs
params.description: Use the absolute value of the key when 1; use signed values when 0.

params.name: size
params.description: Positive width of each key range.

params.name: low
params.description: Center of the lowest magnitude range; code permits zero and requires it to be at most size/2.

params.name: high
params.description: Upper range reference; must be at least low.

params.name: outbase
params.description: Output filename prefix; the rounded range center and .su are appended.

params.name: print
params.description: Set to 1 to report filenames, trace counts, and mean key values.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Double arithmetic, small rounding offsets, integer conversion, and lrint determine range and filename boundaries; lrint depends on the floating-point rounding mode. Reported averages accumulate in input order.
programs.difficulty_reason: It assigns traces to computed ranges and manages a variable set of output files.

test_cases.description: Split on trace number into narrow ranges and report file statistics.
test_cases.command: suplane nt=64 ntr=8 | sucleave key=tracl size=2 low=1 high=5 abs=1 outbase=part_ print=1

test_cases.description: Use signed range handling with an explicitly selected output prefix.
test_cases.command: suplane nt=64 ntr=8 | sucleave key=tracl size=4 low=0 high=8 abs=0 outbase=signed_ print=0

programs.name: sucommand
programs.purpose: Send consecutive groups of traces to separate invocations of a shell command.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: SUCOMMAND - pipe traces having the same key header word to command

params.name: verbose
params.description: Print a header value and gather size for each command invocation.

params.name: key
params.description: Header key used to detect group boundaries.

params.name: command
params.description: Shell command opened as a write pipe for each group; its stdout is inherited.

params.name: dir
params.description: 0 splits on each value change; -1 or 1 selects the documented decreasing or increasing directional grouping.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: For empty input, the return value of the first gettr is ignored and the program still writes the static trace object to the pipe. Output format and numerical behavior depend on the selected shell command.
programs.difficulty_reason: It manages subprocess pipes and groups traces based on typed header comparisons.

test_cases.description: Run the default no-op command separately for each trace-number group.
test_cases.command: suplane nt=64 ntr=6 | sucommand key=tracl command='suop nop' dir=0 verbose=1 > out.su

test_cases.description: Group a monotonic sequence and apply a scale command.
test_cases.command: suplane nt=64 ntr=6 | sucommand key=tracl command='sugain scale=2' dir=1 verbose=0 > out.su

programs.name: sugetgthr
programs.purpose: Read SU files from a directory and concatenate their traces to standard output.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: SUGETGTHR - Gets su files from a directory and put them

params.name: dir
params.description: Directory whose non-dot entries are read as SU files.

params.name: verbose
params.description: Print filenames when set to 1.

params.name: vt
params.description: Use raw variable-length trace reads when nonzero.

params.name: ns
params.description: Output sample count; required only when vt is nonzero.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Directory iteration order is filesystem-dependent. In vt mode, raw reads are not checked for complete headers or samples, and padding uses the input header's ns before it is replaced; malformed input can cause stale data or out-of-bounds access.
programs.difficulty_reason: It traverses a directory and supports both normal SU reads and raw variable-length trace handling.

test_cases.description: Read a directory containing one ordinary SU file.
test_cases.command: mkdir -p gathers && suplane nt=64 ntr=4 > gathers/a.su && sugetgthr dir=gathers verbose=1 vt=0 > out.su

test_cases.description: Pad variable-length input traces to the requested output length.
test_cases.command: mkdir -p gathers_vt && suplane nt=32 ntr=4 > gathers_vt/a.su && sugetgthr dir=gathers_vt vt=1 ns=64 verbose=0 > out.su

programs.name: sugprfb
programs.purpose: Estimate and subtract a sliding pilot first break from GPR traces.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: SUGPRFB - SU program to remove First Breaks from GPR data

params.name: nx
params.description: Number of traces in the pilot stack; an even value is incremented to make it odd.

params.name: fbt
params.description: Number of initial samples used for first-break estimation and removal.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Float stack accumulation and incremental updates, cross-correlation, QR least-squares fitting, and ramp multiplication are order-sensitive. A negative fitted shift causes a read before ym in find_p; other shift-dependent indexing can also access outside the intended arrays. The code does not check that enough traces exist or that fbt fits in each trace, and some small fbt values make the ramp denominator zero.
programs.difficulty_reason: It buffers a sliding trace window and uses cross-correlation and least-squares fitting for each output trace.

test_cases.description: Process a small sliding window with an explicit first-break length.
test_cases.command: suplane nt=64 ntr=12 | sugprfb nx=5 fbt=20 > out.su

test_cases.description: Exercise automatic adjustment of an even window size.
test_cases.command: suplane nt=64 ntr=12 | sugprfb nx=4 fbt=30 > out.su

programs.name: sumatrix
programs.purpose: Assemble trace sample zones into a source-by-receiver matrix of output traces.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: SUMATRIX - Assemble a Matrix of Trace Sample Zones.

params.name: skeyloc
params.description: Header keys identifying source locations.

params.name: sdivider
params.description: One nonzero divider per source key; defaults to 1.0 for each key.

params.name: rkeyloc
params.description: Header keys identifying receiver locations.

params.name: rdivider
params.description: One nonzero divider per receiver key; defaults to 1.0 for each key.

params.name: rfill
params.description: Controls whether missing receiver positions are emitted as zero traces: 0, 1, or 2.

params.name: lenzone
params.description: Zone length in milliseconds, rounded to samples using the first trace's dt.

params.name: numzone
params.description: Number of zones per output trace.

params.name: maxsources
params.description: Maximum number of unique source-key combinations.

params.name: maxreceivers
params.description: Maximum number of unique receiver-key combinations.

params.name: maxtraces
params.description: Maximum number of input traces.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Source and receiver identifiers use floor of double header values divided by double dividers, so boundary rounding matters. Zone length uses float input with double arithmetic and rounding. Default key strings are allocated only 3 bytes before copying four characters plus the terminator, causing heap buffer overflows; insertion into the unique-location pointer arrays can also write one element beyond their allocations. Output sample count and input dt are not safely bounded.
programs.difficulty_reason: It buffers all input zones, sorts unique multidimensional identifiers, and constructs a sparse matrix of output traces.

test_cases.description: Build a small matrix with no empty receiver traces.
test_cases.command: suplane nt=64 ntr=8 | sumatrix skeyloc=tracl rkeyloc=cdp sdivider=1 rdivider=1 lenzone=16 numzone=3 rfill=0 maxsources=16 maxreceivers=16 maxtraces=16 > out.su

test_cases.description: Reverse source ordering and request all receiver positions.
test_cases.command: suplane nt=64 ntr=8 | sumatrix skeyloc=tracl rkeyloc=cdp sdivider=-1 rdivider=1 lenzone=20 numzone=2 rfill=2 maxsources=16 maxreceivers=16 maxtraces=16 > out.su

programs.license_note: Author states that the program was started from surescsv.c for its shot and receiver identifier code.
